J6 9fd4 PUSHED as GERRIT CHANGE 1049 — https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1049
REBASED FIRST, at the operator's prompting, and it settled the open question. origin/main was 7 commits ahead of my working base, and one of them — 6526cfeae '2c38: fix reuse tests under DET short-circuit' — fixed the two test_plan_review_reuse failures I had triaged as pre-existing. After rebasing they PASS. So my ATTRIBUTION was right (they were never mine; I proved it by stashing my work and reproducing them on pristine source) but my CURRENCY was wrong: I baselined against a stale local origin/main without fetching first. Fetch before you baseline — otherwise 'pre-existing on main' can mean 'already fixed on the real main'.
POST-REBASE, full suite: 7903 passed / 29 skipped / 123 deselected / 0 FAILED in 29m45s. make lint GREEN, make typecheck GREEN (398 source files). Nothing over the 800-LOC cap.
Commit: 12 files. Trailers verified, 50/72 hook passed, verify-commit-ticket OK.

WHAT THE HELD-OUT ORACLE BOUGHT ON THIS STORY — a real defect the happy-path spec could not see. transport.py claimed its retry policy 'mirrors acli_rest._rest_urlopen_with_retry exactly' but retried only requests' ConnectionError/Timeout. acli_rest ALSO retries builtin TimeoutError and its docstring records why: 'read-timeout from ssl/socket layer'. Since Python 3.10 socket.timeout IS builtin TimeoutError, so that fault escapes requests' wrappers entirely — DC would have failed a transient error the Cloud path already survives. Verified by reading acli_rest rather than trusting either side, then fixed with the citation inline.
AND THREE OF MY OWN ERRORS, all caught before landing:
 1. My held-out helper invented a kwargs signature for build_client_from_settings; the real seam takes a JiraDataCenterSettings NamedTuple. I had over-specified an internal signature instead of driving the production seam.
 2. A mutation that edited UNREACHABLE code — requests is not installed in this venv, so the retryable-exceptions function takes its ImportError branch and my edit to the other branch did nothing. It 'passed' 9 tests and proved nothing. Caught it because the run took 0.47s when a real retry costs 7s of backoff; redone against the reachable branch, where it correctly failed in 7.37s.
 3. _config_schema.py 797 -> 861, over the module-size cap. Third time this epic a file sitting a few lines under the cap was pushed over by an otherwise-correct change.
On (3) I applied the operator's standing rule that a split must be justified by COHESION, not LOC pressure: rejected shrinking my own addition (the file had no room regardless), rejected moving the validator into the adapter (the module documents itself as a low-level leaf with no rebar.* deps), and split along the seam its OWN DOCSTRING names — extracting the value coercers into _config_coercion.py (189 LOC, over AGENTS.md's 100-LOC floor). ConfigError moved with them because 26 of its 30 raise sites are coercers; _config_schema re-exports it so the public API is unchanged. 360 config tests pass unmodified as the regression evidence.

EPIC: 5 of 8 closed (J1-J5), J6 in review. Remaining: J7 b4e3 (assemble JiraDataCenterBackend + hold it to the backend-agnostic contract suite) then J8 8c35 (the ADR).
